# Growthbook <> Truemeds - Intro
Date: 2026-10-13 | Duration: 36.75m

## Summary
True Meds is seeking to increase experimentation speed because its current platform limits the team to 24 concurrent experiments, requires 1.5 to 2 months per experiment due to low traffic, and lacks Cupid, sequential testing, and long-term holdout capabilities. Growthbook said it supports unlimited experiments, Cupid, sequential testing, multi-armed bandits, power analysis, independent experiment layers, and unified metrics. True Meds is approximately 70% migrated to Snowflake and is comparing Growthbook’s managed event-based model with its warehouse-native experiment-based model. Cost, compute, USD-to-INR currency risk, implementation ease, and execution speed are key decision factors. The team is also renegotiating Mixpanel costs and assessing whether Growthbook could consolidate dashboards. Growthbook proposed a technical deep dive, product demo, and possible proof of concept, with follow-up sessions planned during Indian business hours.

## Keywords
Experimentation, Snowflake, Warehouse-native, Growthbook, Pricing, Analytics integration

## Action Items

**Dan Wathne**
Send follow-up email with proposed agenda and availability for Thursday/Friday sessions to conduct demo and technical integration with Truemeds team (34:00)
Provide ballpark pricing estimates based on expected experiment ramp-up and events tracked for both managed and warehouse-native options (23:15)

**Pranav Chavan**
Coordinate with analytics and technical leads (Arvind and Yash) to join next technical integration and demo session with Growthbook (31:50)
Share event volume, metrics tracked, and provide further info needed for accurate pricing and integration feasibility (23:50)

**Truemeds Analytics & Technical Leads**
Prepare for technical deep dive on Snowflake data warehousing setup, event pipelines, and integration requirements with Growthbook (18:40)

**All Participants**
Prepare questions and requirements especially around feature setup, experiment run management, analytics overlap with Mixpanel, and pricing concerns for next meeting (31:00)

# Growthbook <> TrueMeds - Techincal Demo
Date: 2026-10-15 | Duration: 63.77000045776367m

## Summary
The discussion focused on whether GrowthBook could help expand experimentation beyond the current 24-concurrent-experiment limit toward at least 50, with GrowthBook cited as supporting customers running 100–200 experiments monthly. The team prioritized Snowflake as the single source of truth, avoiding duplicate data stores while using a metrics catalog for standardized and custom metrics. GrowthBook’s post-stratification, custom parameters, Sample Ratio Mismatch checks, namespaces, attributes, and non-overlapping buckets were discussed for managing cohorts such as first-time and repeat users. Feature flags support staged rollouts, guardrail metrics, sticky bucketing, and consistent web/mobile assignment. AI capabilities include explaining experiment outcomes, generating dashboards and reports, and tracking win rates, revenue impact, and lost opportunities. Next steps include an engineering follow-up next week, answers and examples from GrowthBook’s data science team, a trial using historical Snowflake data, and continued pricing discussions against Statsig and Eppo. Sources: discussion points at 09:01–01:00:43.

## Keywords
Experimentation, Feature Flags, Snowflake Integration, Bayesian Statistics, Cohort Stratification, AI Experimentation

## Action Items

**Damacharla Aravind**
Coordinate scheduling follow-up call with TrueMeds engineering team for deeper integration discussion, targeting next week Thursday or Friday (59:00)
Collect and send any additional technical questions from TrueMeds engineering or data teams ahead of the next call to facilitate preparation (01:02:03)

**Dan Wathne**
Follow up via email with TrueMeds team providing clarifications, screenshots from the demo, and scheduling options for next week’s integration call; initiate pricing discussion over email (01:01:00)

**Rémy Marin**
Investigate and clarify GrowthBook’s capability to support dynamic saved groups (buckets) to avoid user overlap between multiple experiments targeting the same cohorts; provide detailed examples and screenshots to TrueMeds (42:00)

**Dan Wathne & Rémy Marin**
Prepare trial environment setup integrating Snowflake data for TrueMeds to test GrowthBook features with historical experiment data (58:00)
